name: The Beautiful Game: From a Sheffield Pitch to Doha
description: How a pastime with rules scribbled in London became the world's biggest sport: clubs, stars, cups and the crowds that made them.

checkpoints.name: Rules and clubs
checkpoints.note: Sheffield F.C. is the oldest club, and the Football Association fixes the laws of association football in 1863. Clubs such as Arsenal, Celtic, Rangers, Liverpool, Manchester United and Juventus grow out of factories, churches and schools. FIFA is set up in 1904.

checkpoints.name: A world game
checkpoints.note: Uruguay hosts and wins the first World Cup in 1930. Real Madrid, FC Barcelona and AC Milan build strong sides, Boca Juniors and Santos grow in South America, and in 1950 the Maracana stadium holds a record crowd.

checkpoints.name: Pelé and the 1960s
checkpoints.note: A young Pelé wins the 1958 World Cup. The old Wembley Stadium sees England win in 1966, Brazil triumph in 1970, and Johan Cruyff's Ajax and the Dutch bring Total Football. Benfica and Bayern Munich rise in Europe, with the European Cup, later the Champions League.

checkpoints.name: Television and tragedy
checkpoints.note: Maradona's 1986 World Cup is a landmark, the Ballon d'Or lists the best players, and Hillsborough forces stadiums to change. The Premier League is formed in 1992 and television money reshapes the sport.

checkpoints.name: Global superclubs
checkpoints.note: Messi and Ronaldo dominate the Ballon d'Or, El Clásico draws a global audience, and the 2002 and 2022 World Cups show football reaching Asia and the Middle East. The Champions League becomes the club game's grandest stage.
